profile.a: The author playing the lending bank in a role-play for Organisations versus Markets, drawing on work in three financial institutions and a consulting project for H&M.
The bank's board and credit committee (Part 1), and the five other role-players: government, H&M's CEO, investor, not-for-profit and politician (Part 2).
Whether the bank should cut interest rates on green loans to H&M, a textile company reducing emissions and waste, while accepting a higher chance of default.
Handed in on 10 January 2025; OKRs run to 2035. The EU textiles strategy dates from March 2022.
UK and EU (H&M Hennes & Mauritz UK Ltd), under the FCA and the European Banking Authority.
Regulators and markets push banks towards green lending, and banks must report their green loans in detail; the fashion sector faces growing sustainability rules.

Freeman's stakeholder theory sorts primary and secondary stakeholders, each one's position is stated, then mitigations (benchmarking, WACC from market betas) and OKRs are set; Part 2 critiques the other roles.

charts.title: Who backs cheaper green loans to H&M
text: For: funding keeps green models alive
charts.takeaway: Support is broad, but the opposition sits exactly where the risk is managed: the executives and the short-term shareholders. That is why the paper answers with guardrails rather than a simple yes.

charts.title: The guardrails the bank sets

items.title: Before approval
items: Full WACC model using market, project and company betas

items.title: Comprehensive risk assessment
items: At least 90% accuracy in statement checks against independent audits

items.title: Monitoring and early warning
items: Real-time flags on revenue drops and cash flow problems
Net interest margin of at least 5% on high-risk loans

items.title: If the risk is too high
items: Renewable energy lending: similar environmental impact at a lower risk rate

charts.takeaway: The tension the paper leaves open: a 5% margin floor on high-risk loans sits awkwardly with a policy of cutting rates for green borrowers.
